seoDescription: Learn the fundamentals of Dependency Injection (DI) in Spring Boot by building a simple Java application from scratch. This tutorial walks through setting up a project using Spring Initializr, explaining the role of the Spring Inversion of Control (IoC) container and how it manages objects (beans). You'll see how to use ApplicationContext to interact with the container and fetch beans, why the @Component annotation is crucial for telling Spring which classes to manage, and how this prevents manual object creation for cleaner code.

chapters.title: Creating a Simple Spring Boot Project
chapters.description: Introduces dependency injection with Spring Boot and walks through creating a new non-web project using Spring Initializr.

chapters.title: Understanding the Spring IoC Container
chapters.description: Explains how `SpringApplication.run()` creates an Inversion of Control (IoC) container within the JVM to manage application objects.

chapters.title: Manual Object Creation vs. The Spring Way
chapters.description: A `Dev` class is created to show the traditional Java approach of manual object instantiation versus the goal of having Spring manage the object.

chapters.title: Fetching a Bean from ApplicationContext
chapters.description: This chapter shows how to get a reference to the `ApplicationContext` and use `getBean()` to request an object, leading to a `NoQualifyingBeanFoundException`.

chapters.title: Telling Spring to Manage a Bean with @Component
chapters.description: The `@Component` annotation is introduced as the way to mark a class as a managed bean, instructing the Spring container to create and manage its object.

chapters.title: Verifying Dependency Injection and Next Steps
chapters.description: The code is successfully executed, demonstrating that Spring is now injecting the `Dev` object, and the video tees up a future topic on multi-level dependencies.
